text:
maya (Docs): quick sync — i'm drafting the docs section that describes how audit logs are stored, redacted, and retained. can security/legal confirm the final phrasing and if we should include an SDK snippet showing retention metadata?
sam (Security): +1, please include the exact phrase we should use. current internal policy link: https://redwood.internal/compliance/log-retention (will post snapshot). default is 90 days for hosted, adjustable for enterprise.
sarah (Legal): avoid absolute promises about deletion. suggested phrasing: "Audit logs are retained for operational and compliance purposes for a configurable period; customers can request retention changes or legal holds." also add: "We may retain copies if required by law."
maya (Docs): thanks sarah — that wording works. do we say "configurable via account settings" or keep it generic?
sam (Security): say "configurable per contract or account settings" so it's clear for dedicated/private customers.
maya (Docs): ok will use: "retained for operational and compliance purposes for a configurable period (default 90 days for hosted). customers on Dedicated or Private can set retention via contract or account settings; legal holds override retention."
devon (SDK): i can add an example TypeScript snippet for the SDK to show how to set retention and redaction level. quick draft:
```ts
// set audit log retention and redaction when creating a dataset
await redwood.audit.createPolicy({
  key: 'payment-events',
  retention_days: 90,
  redaction_level: 'pii-partial', // options: none | pii-partial | pii-full
});
```
devon (SDK): question — field names we use in runtime api are `retention_days` and `redaction_level`, right? alex, does that match the current API?
alex (Eng): names are close. backend expects `retention_ttl_days` not `retention_days` in the persistence layer. we should present the SDK-level names as the friendly ones and map them server-side. for the docs snippet use the SDK names (retention_days) and add a note about internal mapping.
sarah (Legal): include a short sentence about redaction capabilities and limits: "Redaction is best-effort; customers should not assume it is a substitute for avoiding collection of sensitive data."
maya (Docs): adding that. also adding a small example of what a redacted audit event might look like for docs readers.
```json
{
  "event_id": "evt_01F...",
  "user": "[REDACTED]",
  "action": "token.create",
  "details": "--redacted--",
  "retained_until": "2026-06-15T00:00:00Z"
}
```
sam (Security): one ops note: we can't retroactively redact fields that were already exported to downstream sinks (stackdriver, snowflake) without a migration. please add a migration note if we say logs can be redacted after the fact.
maya (Docs): good call. i'll add a migration guide bullet: steps for customers and eng to run a re-redaction job, and a link to the internal migration runbook.
alex (Eng): i'll draft the runbook PR for the migration. quick checklist: 1) identify affected objects 2) run redaction job in a dry-run 3) reconcile diffs 4) apply in batches 5) verify downstream sinks.
devon (SDK): i'll include the SDK test snippet and a sample response for success/failure. e.g. response includes `policy_id` and `effective_retention_days`.
```json
{
  "policy_id": "plc_abc123",
  "effective_retention_days": 90
}
```
maya (Docs): tagging this as a docs PR i'll open later today: will include legal-approved phrasing, SDK snippet, migration note, and links to internal policy + runbook (sarah/sam, please verify links).
sarah (Legal): confirm i will review the PR. tiny edit: change "customers can request retention changes" -> "customers may request retention changes in accordance with their contract".
maya (Docs): noted and updated in the draft.
sam (Security): +thumbsup for the plan. one minor nit: please add a short section on retention export TTL for exports and how long external sinks may keep data.
maya (Docs): added an exports paragraph and a link to the recommended export retention best-practices.
ir-bot: PR created by @maya: https://redwood.internal/pulls/5238 (docs/audit-retention-sdk-examples)
devon (SDK): i'll follow up with a quick patch to ensure SDK maps `retention_days` -> `retention_ttl_days` in the payload.
maya (Docs): perfect — i'll wait for devon's patch and sarah's signoff before merging. thanks everyone :heart:
alex (Eng): adding to eng calendar to coordinate migration run once docs and SDK are live.
sarah (Legal): doing final read now, will leave comments in PR.
maya (Docs): merging plan: wait 48h after SDK release, then merge docs update and ping customers via changelog.
sam (Security): ack. if any compliance customers require earlier notice, we'll handle on a case-by-case basis.
maya (Docs): done for now — will post PR link in #announcements once merged :shipit:
